restatements.text: Requires all public school classrooms to display a poster of the Ten Commandments that is at least 11 by 14 inches and printed in a large, easily readable font.

findings.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster of the Ten Commandments
findings.mechanism: Requires the display of a specific religious text in all public school classrooms.

findings.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster of the Ten Commandments
findings.mechanism: Mandates that public institutions sponsor and display a specific religious text in classrooms.

analysis.answer: Current law does not address religious displays in public school classrooms. The measure changes this by legally requiring every public school classroom to display a poster of the Ten Commandments.
Direct costs include the production, distribution, and installation of the posters for every public school classroom. There may also be significant legal costs if the mandate is challenged in court.

Unless private donations cover the acquisition of the posters, public school districts and taxpayers will bear the cost of purchasing and displaying them, as well as the cost of any resulting litigation.
Schools will need to procure the posters to comply with the mandate. Advocacy groups are likely to initiate legal challenges regarding the separation of church and state.
The text does not state the problem it seeks to address. The mechanism mandates the presence of a specific religious text in the learning environment of public schools.

flags.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster
flags.note: The measure mandates the display of posters but does not provide or identify a funding source to procure them.
The text does not define what specific parameters constitute a large or easily readable font, leaving it open to interpretation.

items.text: Expands religious expression in public institutions by requiring public school classrooms to display the Ten Commandments.
Weakens limits on government religious endorsement by legally mandating the display of a specific religious text in public schools.

changes.empty_reason: The measure does not affect any directional concerns.

items.text: Maintains limits on government religious endorsement by not mandating the display of religious texts in public school classrooms.
Forgoes expanding religious expression in public schools, leaving classrooms without a required display of the Ten Commandments.
